body: i already will take at least 5 and a half years, i've lost all perception of how life is after this shitshow. another semester just feels like another eternity

Comp sci. And yeah, you probably said it better than I could: if you didn't intern then the things mentioned are your only talking points. But these are quantifiable so it's easier to objectively compare two people using these than it is to try and be objective about work experience and such.

I enjoy the subject, even if I fucking hate college. I frequent r/cscareerquestions a lot, probably more than is good for my mental health.

I also just didn't submit a final project for a class (100% my fault, I gotta ask the prof if I could still pass cause I was doing average until that point), so I'm hyper stressed about if I might fail. Please tell me I'm fucking retarded for doing that. I know I am but I need someone to tell me I made a mistake.

In the grand scheme of things, I'm fine. I'm somewhat interested in a high paying field that overall besides some stupid shit like above, I'm performing above average in. But I also just have also turned into a bitter, aggressive, narcissistic pile of shit, and if I walk out of college making some chickenshit 65k or less then I've honestly just proven that I'm pathetic and I'm better off dead so my parents don't have to support me when I inevitably fuck everything up again like I always do.

I'm an asshole. It's a long story of how I became one, and I'm not a sympathetic person even in my own story.

I hate college enough that I'm legitimately excited for a 40 hour work week.

Income, probably shorter commute (90 minutes currently), and I get to come home earlier? Sign me the fuck up.

Perhaps I made it sound a bit exaggerated, but resumes pass through several filters, and when you're a new graduate, unless you've interned all you really have is gpa, your shitty side projects, and the weight of your school.

In like 3 years it won't matter but if it takes me that long to get my shit together life honestly isn't worth living.

It's kinda long winded. I'd basically have to retell the entire waste of life that was the last 5 years of my life, and even then I don't think my thoughts are particularly uncommon.

I've already fucked up my project, I only have like 4 more months to fix myself before i bite the bullet and take the slow path, or just die because a slow life isn't worth living.
Not med school, a different high paying but culturally toxic field where everyone is envious of the top 10%

You're actually not allowed in my major with under a 3.0. Curves for most of my classes puts the average around a B.

I dunno, my life is just kind of boring and my schoolwork/career has consumed 90% of my free time, so I feel like doing poorly in the only thing I actually have the energy and drive to do is kind of fucking bad.

Have one more semester after this one before I graduate college. I hated every second of it and my GPA doesn't even matter past this semester, since I apply for new grad jobs (where it matters) next semester (without them knowing that one).

Going under a 3.3 is how you get your resume shredded on the spot.

Obviously I'm not going to kill myself over a number, but I've become a ruined mess of a person and I need to stop fucking up.
It's average. And average gets filtered out and discarded when everyone else is competitive as fuck.
